sentences.text: Karatausuchus is an extinct genus belonging to the atoposaurid crocodylomorphs, a group within the larger parent group Crocodyliformes.
The skeleton is notable for possessing over 90 teeth, while other anatomical features are hard to identify. This individual specimen was estimated to be 160 mm in length.

The animal is known from a single fossil specimen found in the Karabastau Svita near Mikhailovka in the Karatau Mountains of southern Kazakhstan. The type specimen, cataloged as PIN 25858/1, is a complete but poorly preserved juvenile skeleton that may retain some soft tissue. The genus was described in 1976 by Mikhail Efimov, with the type species named K. sharovi.
Karatausuchus lived during the Oxfordian stage, between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
